Get the rates the denominators use from survey data

Source: R/2_denominators_calculate_indicator_coverage.R
get_national_rates.Rd

Takes the most recent survey value of ANC1 coverage, Penta1 coverage and the stillbirth, neonatal and post-neonatal mortality rates, and converts each to a proportion. A rate the survey data does not have is filled with the value given in the matching argument. The result has the rates that calculate_indicator_coverage() takes as arguments.

Usage

get_national_rates(
  .data,
  admin_level = c("national", "adminlevel_1", "district"),
  anc1survey = .cd_method$denominators$anc1survey,
  dpt1survey = .cd_method$denominators$dpt1survey,
  sbr = .cd_method$denominators$sbr,
  nmr = .cd_method$denominators$nmr,
  pnmr = .cd_method$denominators$pnmr,
  twin = .cd_method$denominators$twin,
  preg_loss = .cd_method$denominators$preg_loss,
  subnational_map = NULL
)

Arguments

.data

A cd_survey_data object with year and r_* columns (r_anc1 and r_penta1 in percent, and optionally r_sbr, r_nmr and r_pnmr per 1,000). National survey data for admin_level = "national", regional survey data (with an adminlevel_1 column) otherwise.

admin_level

Character. The administrative level of the survey data: "national", "adminlevel_1" or "district".

anc1survey

Numeric. ANC1 coverage (a proportion) to use where the survey has no value.

dpt1survey

Numeric. Penta1 coverage (a proportion) to use where the survey has no value.

sbr

Numeric. Stillbirth rate (a proportion) to use where the survey has no value.

nmr

Numeric. Neonatal mortality rate (a proportion) to use where the survey has no value.

pnmr

Numeric. Post-neonatal mortality rate (a proportion) to use where the survey has no value.

twin

Numeric. Twin birth rate (a proportion). It is not read from the survey data, so this value is always the one returned.

preg_loss

Numeric. Pregnancy loss rate (a proportion). It is not read from the survey data, so this value is always the one returned.

subnational_map

Optional. A data frame mapping survey regions to adminlevel_1 units, used for subnational levels. Default is NULL.

Value

A tibble with one row for national data, or one row per unit for subnational data, and the columns pnmr, nmr, sbr, preg_loss, twin, anc1survey and dpt1survey, all as proportions. Subnational results also have the admin column or columns.

Examples

path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core")
cache <- load_cache_data(path)
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths,
#>   ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah
rates <- get_national_rates(cache$national_survey)
rates
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>     pnmr    nmr   sbr preg_loss  twin anc1survey dpt1survey
#>    <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 0.0121 0.0230  0.02      0.03 0.015      0.980      0.971

# A stillbirth rate of your own, used because the survey has none
get_national_rates(cache$national_survey, sbr = 0.015)$sbr
#> [1] 0.015

# The rates of each survey region
regional <- get_national_rates(cache$regional_survey, admin_level = "adminlevel_1")
regional
#> # A tibble: 55 × 8
#>    adminlevel_1       pnmr    nmr   sbr preg_loss  twin anc1survey dpt1survey
